renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: correlation_heatmap
  title: Library correlation
  description: |-
    Each cell is the Spearman correlation between two libraries over the features detected in at least half of them, with libraries ordered by clustering. It answers which libraries resemble each other and which stand apart.
    How to read: blocks of high correlation are libraries of one condition or of neighbouring time points. A library whose row is paler than all others is an outlier, to check for a failed preparation or a swap before any comparison.
    Note: featureCounts publishes no correlation cut-off and no pass mark is drawn.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24227677/
  kind: complex_heatmap
  roles:
    index: sample

- component: table
  title: Library correlation matrix
  description: |-
    Each row is a library and each column the Spearman correlation of its log2 counts per million with another library. It answers the exact correlation behind every cell of the heatmap.
    How to read: read across a row to find the libraries it resembles least.

- component: card
  title: Features counted
  description: |-
    The hero number is the count of distinct features with at least one read in some library, and the bars rank the chromosomes by how many they hold. It answers how many features the count matrix covers and where they sit.
    How to read: the count is the size of the quantified annotation after features with no read anywhere are dropped. A chromosome that leads is gene rich.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24227677/
  column: gene_id
  aggregation: nunique
  aggregations:
  - count
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: chromosome
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: chromosomes with the most features

- component: card
  title: Reads counted over features
  description: |-
    The hero number is the reads assigned to features over every library, and the bar splits them by library, with the median and maximum count of one feature in one library beside it. It answers how much of the total each library contributes.
    How to read: a thin share is a shallow library, whose counts are noisier. Libraries are compared in counts per million below, so depth differences do not distort the comparison.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24227677/
  column: counts
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: composition
  breakdown_col: sample
  caption: counted reads, by library

- component: figure
  title: Counts per million per library
  description: |-
    Each box is a library, with the distribution of log2 counts per million plus one over its features. It answers whether libraries are on a comparable scale after depth is accounted for.
    How to read: boxes at similar heights mean libraries are comparable. A library shifted up or down, or with a very different spread, needs a closer look before any differential analysis.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median log2 counts per million of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Subread.
  visu_type: box
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: log2_cpm
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Library
      log2_cpm: log2 counts per million + 1
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: log2_cpm

- component: interactive
  title: Feature
  description: Filters the dashboard to the features picked here. It answers how a gene or feature behaves
    across libraries.
  interactive_type: MultiSelect
  column_name: gene_id

- component: table
  title: Gene counts
  description: |-
    Each row is a feature in one library, with its position, strand and length, the reads counted, the counts per million and their log2. It answers the exact value behind every other tile.
    How to read: filter by feature to see its counts across libraries, or sort by counts to find the most expressed features.

- component: card
  title: Reads counted over features
  description: |-
    The hero number is the reads assigned to features over every library, and the box shows the spread between libraries. It answers how much usable signal the run holds and how even depth is.
    How to read: a wide box means uneven depth, so compare libraries in counts per million. A library far below the box has too little signal to trust.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/24227677/
  column: assigned_reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: per library, with its spread

- component: card
  title: Features detected
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median count of features reaching ten reads in a library, and the histogram shows how libraries distribute. It answers how complex the libraries are.
    How to read: a library detecting far fewer features than the rest is low in complexity, because of shallow depth or a few dominating transcripts.
  column: genes_detected
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: histogram
  caption: features detected per library, distribution

- component: card
  title: Share held by the top 100 features
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest percent of a library's reads taken by its 100 most counted features, shown against 100 percent. It answers how narrow the most concentrated library is.
    How to read: a narrow library holds most of its reads in a few loci, such as rRNA, and its other features are poorly measured. featureCounts defines no cut-off for this share, so none is drawn.
  column: top100_share_pct
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - median
  - min
  secondary_layout: gauge
  coverage_max: 100.0
  caption: highest library share, of 100

- component: figure
  title: Reads counted over features per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library, with the reads assigned to features. It answers how deep each library is.
    How to read: bars of similar height mean balanced libraries. A short bar is a shallow library that will give noisy counts.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of reads counted over features of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Subread.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: assigned_reads
    color: sample
    labels:
      sample: Library
      assigned_reads: Reads counted over features
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: assigned_reads

- component: figure
  title: Depth against features detected
  description: |-
    Each point is a library, with its counted reads on the horizontal axis and the features detected on the vertical axis, coloured by the share of reads held by its 100 top features. It answers whether more depth buys more features.
    How to read: libraries usually climb together, and a library below the trend detects fewer features than its depth suggests. A high share of the top 100 on the colour scale explains it, as a few loci take the reads.
    Lines and annotations: The dashed line is the median number of features detected of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of Subread.
  visu_type: scatter
  dict_kwargs:
    x: assigned_reads
    y: genes_detected
    color: top100_share_pct
    hover_name: sample
    labels:
      assigned_reads: Reads counted over features
      genes_detected: Features detected
      top100_share_pct: Share of top 100 features (%)
      sample: Library
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: genes_detected

- component: table
  title: Library depth and complexity
  description: |-
    Each row is a library, with the reads counted over features, the features detected and their share, the share of the top 100 features and the median log2 counts per million. It answers the exact numbers behind every other tile and lets a row selection filter the dashboard.
    How to read: sort by the top 100 share to find the narrowest libraries.
  row_selection_enabled: true
  row_selection_column: sample
